newsitem.title: UK: Crude tankers mainly flat, U.K./Cont may slip.
newsitem.headline: Crude tankers mainly flat, U.K./Cont may slip.

text.p: Crude tanker rates were mainly flat on Monday with signs of slippage in the U.K./Continent sector, brokers said.

UKC trips were pegged at W110 for 80,000 tonners but one broker said, "I think it will get a little cheaper. There are quite a lot of modern ships in early positions. They won't all find early cargoes." The Tromso Confidence was reported fixed at W82.5 for a Mongstad-Philadelphia voyage for 137,000 tonnes for Sun, following on from the Knock Sheen at the same rate for 135,000 tonnes from Sullom Voe to the U.S. Gulf for Koch.

In the Middle East, the 1996-built Bourgogne was said fixed at W62 to South Korea with 265,000 tonnes for Hyundai, while a much older vessel, the Astro Gamma, was put at W57.5 for the same tonnage to Singapore for Stentex.

An Italian broker assessed 80,000 tonnes cross-Med at W105, down from W110 late last week, while on fuel oil 25,000 tonnes cross-Med was put at an unchanged W180, and the same tonnage U.K./Cont was around W175, down five points on thin demand.
The Caribs sector, which is often volatile, was mainly flat, with 70,000 tonnes at W155 and 50,000 tonnes at W192.5, brokers said.
But 50,000 tonne Caribs/USAC fuel oil cargoes were fixed slightly higher at W205, against W200 on Friday. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
